title: Extract email addresses from a file
description:
Write a function `extract_emails(path)` that reads the text file at `path` and returns every email address found in it, in the order they appear.

`email_exchanges_big.txt` (a real mailing-list archive, 1138 email addresses) is available in your working directory.
starter_code:
import re


def extract_emails(path):
    # your code here
    pass
hints: An email address has three parts a regular expression can match directly: characters before the @ (letters, digits, dots, plus, hyphen), the @ itself, and a domain made of dot-separated labels after it.
Read the file, then use re.findall() with that pattern to pull out every matching address as a list, in the order they occur in the text.
expected_behavior: Returns every email address found in the file, in order of appearance.
explanation: re.findall() returns every non-overlapping match in the order it finds them in the text, which is exactly the order email addresses appear in the file - no separate loop or index tracking is needed.
